clue.text: Last call from trumpeter?

parts.note: the trumpeter is a kind of swan, and a swan is fabled to sing once, just before it dies

explanation.surface: A bugler sounds the final call of the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trumpeter' points to a brass player, but the trumpeter swan is meant; its last call is the legendary farewell song.
explanation.definitionFit: A final performance or achievement is called this, after the song a dying swan supposedly sings.

clue.text: Ahead in tennis, say, this writer's sympathetic

indicators.note: the word for ahead goes inside the word for a game like tennis

parts.note: tennis is an example of a sport
to be up is to be ahead in a game
the setter speaking: this writer has, I've

explanation.surface: A player leading at tennis says the writer is on their side.
explanation.definitionFit: Being encouraging and on someone's side is a synonym of feeling for their troubles.

clue.text: Current measure a member put together

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A unit of electricity is assembled by an MP.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampere, shortened, is the unit for measuring electrical current.

clue.text: Poet who's stolen girl from pharmacist

indicators.note: the girl's name is stolen away, taken out of the word for the pharmacist

parts.note: a pharmacist dispenses medicines
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A writer of verse has run off with the chemist's daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser was the Elizabethan poet who wrote The Faerie Queene.

clue.text: Old PM, one from Perugia, resident in Morpeth?

parts.note: Lord North was British prime minister during the American War of Independence
Perugia is the capital of the Italian region of Umbria

explanation.surface: A former prime minister of Italian origin now lives in an English market town.
explanation.walkthrough: Morpeth is the county town of Northumberland in north-east England, so its residents are an example of the answer, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living in Morpeth lives in Northumberland, which makes them an example of a native of that county.

clue.text: Forceful nonsense about press employee's retirement

indicators.note: the word for nonsense goes round the other piece

parts.note: rot is nonsense

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a sub is a sub-editor on a newspaper

explanation.surface: A forceful dismissal of claims about a journalist leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong and vigorous, a robust argument is a forceful one.

clue.text: Tragic hero's greeting in Holy Writ

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament
hello is a greeting

explanation.surface: A doomed protagonist's salutation appears in scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moor of Venice is the title character of Shakespeare's tragedy, brought down by jealousy.

clue.text: Humdrum character upset one entering early in year

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the Greek letter is read backwards

parts.note: nu is a Greek letter

indicators.note: the one goes into the phrase for early in the year

parts.note: spring comes early in the year, so the phrase is in spring
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A dull person gets upset when someone arrives at the start of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns NU into UN; 'entering' puts I into IN SPRING, giving IN SP(I)RING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that fails to stir or excite is dull and monotonous, a synonym of humdrum.

clue.text: Make an impact as an archer

definitions.meaning: William ... was the legendary Swiss archer who shot an apple off his son's head

explanation.surface: To have an effect the way a bowman's arrow does.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to have a marked effect, and the name belongs to the Swiss folk hero with the crossbow.

clue.text: Some practise it hand in glove, with no strings attached

definitions.text: Some practise it hand in glove, with no strings attached

parts.words: Some practise it hand in glove, with no strings attached
parts.note: glove puppets are worked by a hand inside, unlike marionettes, which hang on strings

explanation.surface: Reads like partners colluding closely with no conditions on their deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand in glove' and 'no strings attached' are idioms for collusion and unconditional deals, but here they are literal: a hand inside a glove puppet, no marionette strings.
explanation.definitionFit: The craft of working puppets includes glove puppets, operated by a hand rather than by strings.

clue.text: Ear-piercing making end of lobes regularly hurt badly

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word lobes is used
taking every other letter of the word hurt

parts.note: ill can mean badly, as in 'ill treated'

explanation.surface: Having one's ears pierced hurts the lobes badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A high, piercing sound is shrill; ear-piercing describes such a loud, high noise.

clue.text: Insensitive like thieves, committed offence outside King's Head

parts.note: from the idiom 'as thick as thieves', very close

indicators.note: the word for doing wrong goes around the letter

parts.note: sinned means committed an offence

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of King's

explanation.surface: Callous criminals broke the law outside a pub called the King's Head.
explanation.walkthrough: The King's Head is a common British pub name, which disguises the first-letter pick.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not easily hurt by criticism, nor alert to others' feelings, is called this idiomatically.

clue.text: Like one standing for a very long time, fell down for example

definitions.text: Like one standing for a very long time, fell down for example

parts.words: Like one standing for a very long time, fell down for example
parts.note: fells and downs are both kinds of hill, and hills have stood for ages

explanation.surface: Someone who stood for ages eventually collapsed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell down' seems to say someone toppled over; in fact fell and down are both nouns for hills (a northern English moor, a chalk upland in the south).
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means extremely ancient, comparing something's age to that of hills, which have stood for ages.

clue.text: Skilful performer on serious-sounding show

parts.note: a demon is someone very skilled at something, as in a demon bowler

indicators.note: the word for serious is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: straight means serious, as in keeping a straight face

explanation.surface: A virtuoso puts on a solemn-seeming exhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: To show how something works is to illustrate it by example, a direct synonym.

clue.text: He's a deeply disturbed, dozy type

indicators.note: disturbed letters are shaken out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sleeper roused from deep slumber is groggy.
explanation.definitionFit: A drowsy person, often a child who has just woken, is affectionately called this.

clue.text: Fearful old American leaving for Asian island

indicators.note: the old American departs, taken out of the word for fearful

parts.note: timorous means fearful
US is the United States, so American

explanation.surface: A nervous elderly American departs for an island in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: This island in the Malay Archipelago is shared between Indonesia and East Timor.

clue.text: Like bacteria, I claim, distributed round mug

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the word for mug
distributed letters are spread out and reordered

parts.note: to mug someone is to rob them

explanation.surface: Someone claims germs were spread on a cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' looks like a cup in the surface, but it is a verb here: to mug someone is to rob them.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacteria are microbes, so something resembling or caused by them is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Unknown invaders trashed plantations

indicators.note: something trashed is wrecked, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: Mysterious invaders wrecked the crops.
explanation.definitionFit: Grapevine plantations are where wine grapes are grown, so they are a kind of plantation.

clue.text: US city's extended period entertaining Queen

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold within, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: yonks is British slang for a very long time
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: An American town has hosted the monarch for a long stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: YONKS is informal British for ages, as in 'I haven't seen her for yonks'.
explanation.definitionFit: This city in Westchester County, New York, just north of the Bronx, is an example of an American city.

clue.text: Pungent pod reportedly produced in this country?

indicators.note: reported speech means the word is heard, not read

parts.note: a chilli is a hot pepper pod

explanation.surface: Hot peppers are said to be grown in a particular nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works whole: chillies are indeed grown in the South American country, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The long, narrow South American nation is the country in question, referred to as 'this country'.

clue.text: Blushing boy associated with a lot of wrongdoing

indicators.note: a lot of a word is most of it, with the last letter removed

parts.note: crime is wrongdoing
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A lad goes red after being linked with much misbehaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep red colour, and someone who blushes turns that shade, as in 'he went crimson'.

clue.text: In teasing manner, volunteers translated Latin one by one

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

indicators.note: translated here means moved into a different form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: singly means one at a time

explanation.surface: Volunteers tease a learner by rendering Latin word by word.
explanation.definitionFit: Teasing someone with something desired but withheld is to tantalise them; this adverb describes that tormenting manner.

clue.text: Strike-breaker gets method of payment set up

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means raised, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: BACS is the UK bank system for automated payments

explanation.surface: A worker crossing the picket line gets a new way of being paid.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker who carries on during a strike is called a scab, a derogatory term for a blackleg.

clue.text: Chicken-hearted bird with chicken's head

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a raven is a bird

explanation.surface: A cowardly bird has a chicken's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cowardly, as one with a chicken's heart is, is the meaning of this adjective.

clue.text: A compiler from Bangor stopped early for a drink

parts.note: Bangor in County Down is in Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI

indicators.note: the word stops before its final letter

parts.note: a crossword compiler is a setter

explanation.surface: A crossword maker from Bangor knocked off early to go for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: There is also a Bangor in Wales, but the abbreviation needed is NI for Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: This anise-flavoured liqueur is an example of an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: It sounds like company — excessively

indicators.note: signals that a word is heard rather than written

parts.note: from the saying 'two's company, three's a crowd'

explanation.surface: A remark that company is overdone.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means to an excessive degree, as in 'too much'.

clue.text: Confront leader of armada occupying French naval base

indicators.note: the first letter occupies, sits inside, the port's name

parts.note: Brest in Brittany is a major French naval port

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A fleet commander confronts the enemy at a French port.
explanation.definitionFit: To breast a challenge is to face it head on, as a swimmer breasts the waves.

clue.text: Like teeth lecturer featured in books and old papers

indicators.note: the lecturer appears inside the books abbreviation

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
a don is a university lecturer
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: A tutor appears in old books and documents.
explanation.definitionFit: From the Greek for tooth, this adjective means tooth-shaped, as in the odontoid peg of the second vertebra.
